description: Serialized two-row rim preset table (SUPERARMOR, HYPERARMOR). The reconstruction verifies the row struct, one loaded UDataTable, and manager caching at +0x820; no C++ consumer reads a row or its fields, so runtime application of these values is unverified.

ID.simple: Rim preset row key (exported: SUPERARMOR, HYPERARMOR).
ID.technical: FName declared in FGameDataTableRow_MaterialRim and serialized as ImportKeyField 'Id'; retail layout puts it at 0x08. The reconstructed constructor leaves Id to FName's default (NAME_None). StartInitialLoading adds a DataTable primary-asset loader named 'MaterialRimDataTable' (line 433; loaders are created at line 488). After all loaders complete, Tick resolves that loader and appends the loaded UDataTable to MaterialRimDataTables (+0x820) at line 260. There is no FindRow/FindRowInline call for this array or row type, and the exported key strings do not occur in C++ source; no lookup condition, precedence, or sentinel behavior is established.

Color.technical: FVector at retail offset 0x10; constructor default FVector::ZeroVector. Both rows override it: SUPERARMOR (1.0, 1.0, 0.0), HYPERARMOR (0.8, 0.2, 0.2). The catalog and export expose X/Y/Z as double components, but no consumer proves an X/Y/Z-to-RGB conversion for this table. Character, shikigami and weapon material controllers independently cache material parameters named RimColor (GameCharacterMaterialController.cpp:173-178, GameShikigamiMaterialController.cpp:40-45, GameWeaponMaterialController.cpp:116-121); no C++ path connects a MaterialRim row's Color to those caches.

Intensity.technical: float at retail offset 0x28; 5.0 in both exported rows; constructor default 0.0. No reconstructed consumer reads this field, so its scale, clamping and units are not established.

Offset.technical: float at retail offset 0x2C; 0.5 in both exported rows; constructor default 0.0. Material controllers cache a separate RimOffset scalar parameter, and action code animates ShadowRimOffset with hard-coded or character-unique values (for example CN_070_Actions.cpp:541 passes -1.0 and 0.0), but none reads this row field. No consumer establishes the quantity, range, or sign convention.

FadeInTime.technical: float at retail offset 0x30; 0.0 in both exported rows; constructor default 0.0. No row consumer exists, so the units and whether zero means an immediate change are not proven here.

FadeOutTime.technical: float at retail offset 0x34; 0.2 in both exported rows; constructor default 0.0. No row consumer exists, so the units and any reset behavior are not proven here.

notes: Export coverage is one DataTable asset with no numbered shards: the catalog lists one variant, the registry summary has one /Game/DataTables/MaterialRimDataTable entry, and the export has two unique keys (SUPERARMOR, HYPERARMOR) with ImportKeyField 'Id'. The loader registers only 'MaterialRimDataTable', so MaterialRimDataTables receives one loaded UDataTable.

Retail-derived layout evidence pins a 56-byte (0x38) row: Id 0x08, Color 0x10, Intensity 0x28, Offset 0x2C, FadeInTime 0x30, FadeOutTime 0x34 (Tools/verify/layout-checks/AbramsDataTable-LayoutCheckM1.cpp:1200-1205). The retail TCppStructOps::Construct at 0x16c5df0 is recorded as MATCH in status/verdicts.json:50858.

Searches of Source and Plugins for MaterialRim, MaterialRimDataTables, FGameDataTableRow_MaterialRim, exact row keys, RimColor/RimOffset/ShadowRimOffset names, Start*/Set*/Reset* rim symbols, and manager FindRowInline instantiations found only the loader, member declaration, row struct/constructor, and unrelated material-parameter or action code. No row lookup, per-field read, cache alias, or manager accessor was found.

Do not conflate this table with MaterialOutlineDataTable: the outline keys are SUPER_ARMOR/HYPER_ARMOR, which character C++ explicitly maps from status bits to AddOutline/RemoveOutline (GameCharacter.cpp:323-334). No MaterialRim field stores a cross-table key or references those names.

Retail Blueprint assets were not used as evidence here (the project guide records that Blueprints contain no logic). The absence of a traced C++ consumer is therefore an evidence gap, not proof that retail never uses the table; no retail Blueprint or sequencer binding is claimed.

usages.detail: StartInitialLoading builds the DataTable loader name list ('MaterialRimDataTable' at line 433) and creates the primary-asset loaders at line 488; it does not itself resolve the table.

Inside AGameDataTableManager::Tick (line 168), after StudioLoadFlag_B90 is set and all loaders complete, the loader is resolved to a UDataTable and AddLoadedDataTables appends non-null instances to MaterialRimDataTables (+0x820, declared in GameDataTableManager.h:171).
Retail-derived static assertions pin every serialized field offset and the row layout; this is structural evidence only, not a behavioural consumer.
